recognize_zh: 胸部正面（A）與側面（B）X 光的箭頭指向胸椎，C 為脊椎矢狀重組影像，虛線箭頭處可見椎體上下終板中央呈方形凹陷、形成「H 形／魚嘴狀」椎體（H-shaped vertebrae），這是鐮刀型貧血骨梗塞造成的典型影像。
features: Composite radiology figure: PA chest radiograph (A), lateral chest radiograph (B) and sagittal spine image (C)
Arrows in A and B point to thoracic vertebral bodies with endplate deformity
Central step-like depressions of the superior and inferior endplates producing H-shaped (Lincoln log) vertebrae, best seen in C (dashed arrow)
Deformity involves multiple contiguous vertebral levels
Lungs appear clear without large focal consolidation in this image
Cellular morphology is not applicable to this image type
describe_en: Composite figure shows PA and lateral chest radiographs and a sagittal image of the spine. Multiple thoracic vertebral bodies demonstrate central, step-like depressions of the superior and inferior endplates with preserved peripheral margins, producing H-shaped ('fish mouth' or Lincoln log) vertebrae, most clearly seen on the sagittal image. No large focal pulmonary consolidation is evident on these views. This is a radiologic image and no cellular morphology is assessable. Findings are consistent with sickle cell spine, caused by microvascular occlusion and infarction of the central endplate supplied by end-arteries with continued peripheral growth.

ddx.vs: Show smooth, gently curved concave endplate deformity rather than sharply marginated central square step-like depressions.
Gaucher can also produce H-shaped vertebrae, and thalassemia shows coarse trabeculae and marrow expansion, so hemoglobin electrophoresis and clinical context are needed to separate them.
Are focal, irregular intravertebral disc herniations, often with anterior wedging, rather than symmetric central endplate depressions across many levels.
